questions.q: What is the Salesforce Extension Pack in VS Code, fundamentally?
options: A standalone tool that replaces the Salesforce CLI entirely
A set of extensions that wrap the same sf CLI commands as command-palette actions, plus language tooling for Apex, LWC, and more
A cloud-hosted IDE with no local installation needed
A Salesforce Setup menu item, unrelated to VS Code
questions.explain: The Extension Pack wraps the same sf CLI commands you'd run from a terminal, surfaced as command-palette actions and menu items, alongside language-specific tooling for Apex, LWC, Visualforce, Aura, and SOQL.

questions.q: Which extension in the pack provides the glue connecting all the others to your installed CLI?
options: Visualforce
SOQL
Salesforce CLI Integration
Aura Components
questions.explain: Salesforce CLI Integration is the glue extension that lets the rest of the pack call into your installed sf CLI — without the CLI already installed, none of the rest works.

questions.q: What does the Apex Replay Debugger let you do that a plain deploy doesn't?
options: Step through a captured Apex execution log line by line inside the editor to understand what a transaction actually did
Automatically fix failing Apex tests
Deploy Apex classes without any API version specified
Convert Apex code into Lightning Web Components
questions.explain: The Apex Replay Debugger steps through a previously captured debug log line by line inside VS Code, letting you understand exactly what a trigger or Flow-invoked Apex method did during a specific transaction.

questions.q: What must be installed and configured on your machine, beyond the Salesforce CLI, for Apex-related VS Code extension features to work?
options: A Python interpreter
A Java Development Kit (JDK), since the Apex language server and Replay Debugger run on the JVM
Docker Desktop
A second Salesforce CLI installation
questions.explain: Apex autocomplete and the Replay Debugger both depend on a JDK, since they run on the JVM; a missing or misconfigured JDK is the most common cause of those features silently failing to start.

questions.q: Right-clicking a specific file in VS Code's Explorer and choosing a deploy action is functionally equivalent to running which CLI pattern?
options: sf org create scratch with no flags
sf project deploy start with --source-dir set to that file's path
sf project retrieve start with no flags at all
sf package version create
questions.explain: Scoping a deploy action to a specific right-clicked file or folder in VS Code is functionally identical to passing --source-dir with that same path to sf project deploy start on the command line.
